item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft PowerPoint: Publish and unpublish controls for official brand kits
item.description:
[What and why]

We're introducing publish and unpublish controls for Official Brand Kits in Microsoft PowerPoint. This update gives Brand Managers greater control over the lifecycle and availability of brand assets within their organization.

With these new controls, Brand Managers can temporarily remove a Brand Kit from end user access without deleting it or changing editor permissions. When the Brand Kit is ready to be used again, it can be republished. This flexibility helps organizations manage brand content more effectively and ensure only current, approved brand assets are available to users.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 and expected to complete in mid-October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Official Brand Kits in Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Users assigned as Brand Managers
  • Users who access and use published Official Brand Kits

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Official Brand Kits

What will happen

  • Brand Managers will be able to publish and unpublish Official Brand Kits. 
  • When a Brand Kit is unpublished, users will no longer be able to discover or use the Brand Kit.
  • Unpublishing a Brand Kit does not delete the Brand Kit.
  • Existing editor permissions and management access remain unchanged when a Brand Kit is unpublished.
  • Brand Managers can republish a previously unpublished Brand Kit when it is ready to be made available again.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform Brand Managers about the new publish and unpublish controls.
  • Review your organization's processes for determining when Official Brand Kits should be available to users.
  • Update internal documentation or governance guidance for brand asset management, if applicable.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Customize file extensions blocked by Weaponizable File Protection
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is expanding admin controls for Weaponizable File Protection. Admins will be able to customize which file extensions are blocked in Teams based on their organization’s security needs or continue using the Microsoft-recommended default list. This change provides greater flexibility to tailor file protection policies while maintaining a secure collaboration experience.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that use Weaponizable File Protection in Microsoft Teams

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams

What will happen

  • Before this rollout, Microsoft defines the file extensions blocked by Weaponizable File Protection, and admins cannot customize the list.
  • After this rollout, admins can define which file extensions are blocked for their organization or continue using the Microsoft-recommended default list.
  • Organizations with Weaponizable File Protection enabled will continue using the Microsoft-recommended list by default.
  • Organizations that continue using the Microsoft-recommended list will automatically receive future updates to that list.
  • If an admin customizes the list, the organization will use the customized list and will no longer automatically receive future updates to the Microsoft-recommended list.
  • The user experience will not change. Files with blocked extensions will continue to be blocked in Teams as they are today.

Screenshot 1 Customize file type view: 

Screenshot 2 Customize file type add view:

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. Organizations with Weaponizable File Protection enabled will continue using the Microsoft-recommended list by default.

If your organization wants to customize Weaponizable File Protection:

  • Admins can add or remove file extensions based on their organization’s security needs.
  • Admins can reset the configuration to the Microsoft-recommended default list at any time to resume receiving automatic updates.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins will be able to customize the file extensions blocked by Weaponizable File Protection or use the Microsoft-recommended default list.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Legal plugins in Word and Cowork
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft 365 Copilot is introducing legal plugins in Word and Cowork. These plugins provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents. They can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources, helping legal professionals complete legal work in the Microsoft 365 experiences they already use.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout began in late April 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot commercial licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Word desktop
  • Cowork

What will happen

  • Legal plugins in Copilot provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
  • The plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources.
  • The legal capabilities include more than 20 purpose-built legal skills.
  • In Word desktop, the legal plugin is enabled by default. When enabled, Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks in Word.
  • In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks.
  • The legal skills can help users review contracts against playbooks, draft contracts using templates and precedent agreements, compare contracts with precedents, templates, and policies, and explain tracked changes.
  • The Legal Agent is being retired. Existing Legal Agent users will lose access to the product.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin setup is required.

If your organization plans to use the legal plugins:

  • Ensure Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are assigned to eligible users.
  • Review internal legal workflows that may benefit from these capabilities.
  • Communicate these capabilities to your legal teams.
  • Update internal documentation or help desk guidance as appropriate.
  • Instruct legal team users to add the legal plugin in Cowork.
  • Instruct legal team users to use legal skills in Copilot in Word desktop.

If your organization does not plan to use the legal plugins:

  • Turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center to disable the legal plugin in Word for all users.
  • Turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center to disable the plugin in Cowork for all users.

Learn more

  • Manage Copilot for legal - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. The legal plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 to support legal tasks. The supplied source does not specify changes to data storage or caching.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Legal capabilities previously released as the Legal Agent are being made available as legal plugins in Word and Cowork. They provide purpose-built legal skills and can use work context from Microsoft 365.
Does the change provide users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can use purpose-built legal skills in Copilot in Word and Cowork to summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
Does the change add integration with third-party software products?Yes. The legal plugins can connect to supported third-party legal sources. The supplied sources do not identify specific third-party products.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins can turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The supplied source does not specify whether these controls support Entra ID group membership.
Does the change allow a user to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before using its legal skills. The supplied source does not state that users can independently disable the Word legal plugin.

item.title: [planForChange] Support for Office LTSC 2021 and additional apps ended on October 13, 2026
item.description:
[What and Why:]

As previously communicated, support for Office LTSC 2021 ended on October 13, 2026. Microsoft no longer provides security updates, bug fixes, or technical support for this version of Office. Although the applications may continue to function, using unsupported software could expose your organization to potential security and compliance risks, system incompatibilities, and other issues.

Support for Visio LTSC 2021, Project LTSC 2021, and several other products also ended on October 13, 2026. Organizations that continue to use these products should transition to a supported version as soon as possible to receive ongoing security updates, bug fixes, and technical support.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Support for Office LTSC 2021, Visio LTSC 2021, Project LTSC 2021, and other affected products ended on October 13, 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Devices running Office LTSC 2021 or another affected product no longer receive security updates, bug fixes, or technical assistance. The applications do not automatically stop working, but continued use of unsupported software may increase your organization's exposure to security and compliance risks and could result in compatibility or reliability issues.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Identify any devices in your organization that are still running Office LTSC 2021 or another affected product and move them to a supported solution.

For most organizations, we recommend upgrading devices to a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 suite that includes Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise or Microsoft 365 Apps for business. Microsoft 365 Apps provides always-up-to-date versions of familiar apps like Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for desktop, mobile, and web with continuous support under the Modern Lifecycle Policy, and is eligible for use with Microsoft Copilot.

  • Enterprises should review Microsoft 365 E3, Office 365 E3, or Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
  • Organizations with fewer than 300 users should review Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Microsoft 365 Business Standard, or Microsoft 365 Apps for business.

For scenarios that require a fully disconnected solution, we recommend upgrading to Office LTSC 2024. Office LTSC 2024 is Microsoft's current supported on-premises version of Office for commercial customers and is supported until October 2029 under the Fixed Lifecycle Policy.

Resources:

  • Read the upgrade guidance for an overview of how to move from Office LTSC 2021 to Microsoft 365 Apps.
  • Consider engaging Microsoft FastTrack, a Microsoft support service, for moving to Microsoft 365.

Take action now to help maintain security, compliance, and access to supported Office apps.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable any Microsoft 365 service capability?Yes. Support for Office LTSC 2021 and other affected products ended on October 13, 2026. Organizations should move to supported versions to receive ongoing updates and support.
Does the change require admin action?Yes. Admins should identify affected devices and move them to a supported Microsoft 365 Apps, Office, Visio, or Project version as appropriate.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Edge: Browser-native XSLT will be disabled by default
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Edge is deprecating browser-native Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations (XSLT). Edge will disable the XSLTProcessor JavaScript API and XML processing instructions that reference XSLT stylesheets by default. XML processing instructions that reference CSS stylesheets are not affected.

The native XSLT implementation depends on an aging native codebase that processes untrusted XML and XSLT content. Removing this functionality reduces the browser attack surface. XSLT also has low modern web usage, and safer migration alternatives are available.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Organizations may be affected if internal websites, public websites, embedded-device interfaces, or third-party web applications depend on browser-native XSLT. In Microsoft Edge 159, browser-native XSLT will be off by default in Stable. The temporary XSLTEnabled policy is planned for removal in Microsoft Edge 176 in Summer 2027.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Before Microsoft Edge Stable 159, identify applications that use the XSLTProcessor JavaScript API or XML processing instructions that reference XSL stylesheets. To check for browser-native XSLT usage with Lighthouse in Microsoft Edge:

  1. Open the application in a current version of Microsoft Edge.
  2. Sign in and navigate to the application page you want to test.
  3. Open Edge DevTools with F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I.
  4. Select the Lighthouse tool. If it isn't visible, select More tools (+) > Lighthouse.
  5. Select:
    • Mode: Navigation
    • Category: Best Practices
  6. For authenticated applications: In Lighthouse Settings, turn off Clear storage so the audit preserves your signed-in session. Leave it enabled for public pages that don't require stored application state.
  7. Select Analyze page load.
  8. In the report:
    • Search for XSLT, deprecated, or XSLTProcessor.
    • Check for Uses deprecated APIs.
    • Expand Issues were logged in the DevTools Issues panel.
  9. Check the DevTools Issues and Console tools for XSLT deprecation warnings.
  10. Repeat the audit for each relevant page and exercise important application workflows.

Migrate affected applications to supported alternatives or contact the developers/vendor responsible for the affected site to update the application and remove its dependency on browser-native XSLT. If more time is needed, configure the temporary XSLTEnabled policy while application owners complete migration.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins can temporarily use the XSLTEnabled policy to manage XSLT behavior while migrating affected applications.
Does the change modify or disable a capability?Yes. Browser-native XSLT will be disabled by default and the temporary policy is planned for removal in a future Edge release.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Organizations can enhance meeting security with synthetic audio and video detection solutions provided by certified third-party providers. Third-party detection solutions analyze meeting media for signs of synthetic or manipulated audio and video and send detection signals to Teams, enabling integrated in-meeting experiences and controls.

Important: Synthetic media detection is performed by the third-party provider. Microsoft Teams provides the platform integration and experiences for surfacing and acting on detection signals from supported providers.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 573451.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Organizations can choose and integrate certified third-party deepfake detection solutions into Microsoft Teams meetings, helping protect users from emerging AI-generated voice and video threats. This gives customers more flexibility to meet security and compliance needs while enabling users to make more informed trust decisions during meetings.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

To use third-party Synthetic Audio and Video Detection in Microsoft Teams, administrators should evaluate and select a supported detection provider, deploy the provider app through Manage apps in the Teams admin center, grant required permissions, and configure applicable Teams meeting policies.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Certified third-party providers may analyze meeting audio/video signals for synthetic media detection. Review provider terms, data handling, and compliance documentation before enabling.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins manage provider app deployment, permissions, and Teams meeting policy configuration.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Viva Engage: Community feeds improvements
item.description:
Updated October 15, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.   

[Introduction:]

We’re introducing a simpler way to view conversations in Viva Engage communities, organized by recent posts rather than recent activity. This new view is designed to make it easier for users to follow discussions and will be available as an option, alongside the current system, for those who prefer sorting by recent activity and filtering to new conversations only.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 513275.

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in October 2026 and expect to complete by the end of October 2026. 

[How this will affect your organization:]

This change should align better with how people expect to browse and engage with content in their communities, while still preserving the triage flow for those who prefer it.

Who is affected: All Viva Engage users in your organization.

Current experience:

  • Communities default to “new” and “recent activity” if there’s any new content (posts or replies).
  • If there’s no new content, the feed falls back to “all.”
  • Unread indicators on content only exist in the “new” feed.

New experience:

  • The feature will be ON by default.
  • Communities will default to “all” and “recent posts”:

  • Unread indicators will exist in both the “new” and “all” feeds.
  • A sticky user preference will be introduced:
    • If someone changes the feed (new/all) or sort order (recent posts/recent activity), we will maintain that setting across their communities.
    • If someone picks “new” and there’s no new content in the next community, we will fall back to “all” for that community visit, but “new” will remain the preference for that user.

[What you can do to prepare:]

No action is required.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams Rooms: Identify in-room participants with IntelliFrame people labels
item.description:
Updated October 15, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

We're introducing IntelliFrame people labels in Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows to improve meeting clarity and inclusivity for remote participants. When enabled, this feature identifies in-room participants by name and displays a contact card, helping remote attendees easily recognize speakers and follow conversations.

This enhancement supports better hybrid meeting experiences by connecting in-room and remote participants more effectively, improving collaboration and productivity.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 566700.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning late January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026) expected to complete by early February 2027 (previously mid-December 2026)

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows with Teams Rooms Pro licenses
  • In-room participants who have enrolled in voice and face recognition (People Recognition)

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams Rooms on Windows devices
  • Supported intelligent camera hardware

What will happen:

  • IntelliFrame will display name labels under identified in-room participants’ video feeds.
  • Remote participants can select a label to view a contact card with organizational details.
  • The feature is enabled automatically when prerequisites are met.
  • Existing Teams meeting policies for voice and face enrollment are honored.
  • Participants without enrolled profiles will appear without labels.
  • No change occurs if voice and face enrollment is disabled in your organization.

Screenshot - IntelliFrame people labels identify enrolled in-room participants by name, helping remote attendees recognize who's speaking; selecting a label opens the person's contact card

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required to enable this feature.

To maximize value, administrators may:

  • Review and confirm Teams Rooms devices:
    • Ensure devices are licensed with Teams Rooms Pro.
    • Verify use of supported intelligent cameras.
  • Review and update meeting policies:
    • Allow enrollment: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Enabled.
    • Enable name display in rooms: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride On.
  • Encourage users to enroll in voice and face recognition: Teams > Settings > Recognition.
  • Update internal documentation and helpdesk guidance.
  • Notify users about this capability to drive awareness and adoption.

To disable IntelliFrame people labels, administrators can:

  • Turn off in-room name display (labels stop; other IntelliFrame framing unaffected): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride Off
  • Block voice and face enrollment entirely (no one can be identified by name): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Disabled
  • Individual users can opt out anytime by removing their profile in Teams > Settings > Recognition.

Learn more: 

  • What is Microsoft Multi-Stream IntelliFrame and Intelligent Camera? | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)
  • Enable People Recognition on Teams Rooms (voice & face policies) | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)
  • Overview and configuration of voice and face enrollment | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)

[Compliance considerations:]

Compliance AreaImpact
Introduces or modifies AI/ML capabilitiesUses AI-based biometric identification (voice and face profiles) to identify in-room participants. Identification occurs only for users who have consented and completed People Recognition enrollment.
Stores new customer dataThis feature does not create new data; it relies on existing voice and face profiles from People Recognition enrollment, governed by the organization’s current configuration.
Alters processing of existing customer dataParticipant identity data is processed differently when recognition is enabled.
Provides new way of communicating between usersLabels and contact cards enhance visibility of in-room participants for remote users.
Adds or changes admin controlsControlled via Teams meeting policies (EnrollUserOverride and RoomPeopleNameUserOverride).
Allows users to enable/disable the featureUsers can enroll or opt out of voice and face profiles in Teams settings.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Planner: Capacity view
item.description:
Updated October 15, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Capacity view is a new view in Planner that presents a live staffing matrix built from existing Planner task data. It shows a timeline of who is working on what, so team leads can see how work is distributed across the team and spot overallocation or open capacity at a glance, without exporting data or building a separate report. This keeps resource decisions in the same tool where the work is already tracked.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 (previously early October) and expected to complete late October 2026 (previously mid-October)
  • General availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late October 2026 (previously mid-October) and expected to complete by early November 2026 (previously late October)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Planner Plan 3 license in Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) environments 
  • Users without a Plan 3 license will not see Capacity view

Platforms and services

  • Planner in Teams (web and desktop)
  • Planner in Outlook (web and desktop)
  • Capacity view is not included on mobile

What will happen

  • Capacity view appears as a new view on existing plans, alongside Board, Grid, and Schedule.
  • The view is populated entirely from existing Planner task data. No new data is created.
  • Accuracy depends on tasks having assignees and start and finish dates. Tasks missing either will not be represented reliably in the timeline.
  • The view is on by default for eligible users and there is no admin control to disable it. 

[Action required and recommendations]

  • No admin action is required to enable or prepare for this change. To get value from the view, consider the following:
  • Notify Planner users that a new Capacity view will appear on their plans in early October 2026.
  • Update internal training material and Planner guidance to include the new view.
  • Encourage plan owners and team leads to keep assignees and start and finish dates current so the view reflects actual workload.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Planner: Planner Agent chat in basic plans
item.description:
Updated October 15, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Planner Agent chat is coming to Microsoft Planner basic plans. This feature brings Planner Agent directly into the Planner experience, allowing users to ask questions about their plans, understand priorities, and take action without leaving Planner.

Planner Agent chat helps users stay organized by providing quick access to plan status, work that requires attention, and actionable insights. It can also help users create and manage plans using information from Microsoft 365 resources.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 567671.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in early September 2026 (previously late August) and expected to complete by mid-September 2026 (previously early September)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-September 2026 (previously late August) and expected to complete by end of October 2026 (previously late September)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license
  • Organizations that allow access to Planner Agent

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Planner
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Web

What will happen

Eligible users will be able to access Planner Agent chat directly within Planner while working in basic plans.

Users will be able to:

  • Ask questions about plan status, priorities, and upcoming work.
  • Apply AI-generated filters to identify important work more quickly.
  • Use interactive task cards to draft updates, review tasks, and track progress.
  • Receive insights about high-priority work, upcoming deadlines, and at-risk tasks.
  • Create new Planner plans organized by goals and buckets.
  • Use information from Microsoft 365 resources such as emails, meetings, and files when working with Planner Agent.
  • Use natural language prompts such as: "Show me my recent high-priority tasks and what is due this week."

[Action required and recommendations]

Review whether your organization wants users to have access to Planner Agent.

Confirm that users who should use this feature have an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

  • Review Planner Agent settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • If Planner Agent is blocked, users will not have access to this capability.
  • Update internal documentation and user guidance as appropriate.

No additional action is required before rollout.

Learn more

  • Chat with Planner Agent in basic plans | Microsoft Support
  • Manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center | Microsoft 365 admin center | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. This feature introduces Planner Agent chat, an AI-powered experience that interacts with Planner data and can use existing Microsoft 365 resources, including emails, meetings, and files, to provide insights, answer questions, and help users take action.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Planner Agent chat using natural language prompts to analyze plans, identify priorities, create plans, manage tasks, and receive AI-generated insights directly within Planner.
Does this change alter how existing customer data is accessed or processed?Yes. Planner Agent chat can access and process existing Planner data and Microsoft 365 content that users already have permission to access in order to generate responses, recommendations, and insights.
Is there an administrative control available for this feature?Yes. Administrators can control access to this capability through agent settings. Blocking the Planner Agent removes access to the feature.
Can this feature be enabled or disabled by administrators?Yes. Administrators can manage availability of the feature through Planner Agent configuration and access controls.
Does this change affect how users access information within Microsoft 365?Yes. Users gain a new conversational interface that enables them to access and interact with Planner information and related Microsoft 365 content through natural language requests.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Video sharing from OneDrive in Teams events
item.description:
Updated October 15, 2026: We have updated the timeline. If you are a tenant in a GCCH or DoD environment, you can safely ignore this message as you are not impacted. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams will soon support sharing video directly from OneDrive during Teams events. Organizers and producers using Manage what attendees see can load videos from OneDrive and present them on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos in PowerPoint. This improvement provides smoother, higher-quality video playback for attendees and simplifies event production through built-in video playback controls.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early November 2026 and end in early December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Teams event organizers and producers using events configured with Manage what attendees see.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • OneDrive
  • Teams events

What will happen

  • Organizers and producers will be able to select and share videos stored in OneDrive directly within Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see and will have access to built-in controls to start and pause video playback during events.
  • Videos can be presented on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos into a PowerPoint presentation.
  • Attendees will experience smoother and higher-quality video playback.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Facilitator proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps in meetings
item.description:

[What and Why]

We are introducing a new Microsoft Teams Facilitator capability that proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps during meetings. Facilitator can identify when participants ask questions or express uncertainty and retrieve and share relevant answers using web search in the meeting chat. This enhancement helps improve meeting productivity by reducing interruptions and enabling teams to stay focused on goals while accessing needed information. If a participant asks a factual question and no one responds, Facilitator can provide an answer directly in the meeting chat.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558341.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early December 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expected to complete mid-January 2027 (previously mid-December 2026)

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Users in Microsoft Teams meetings where Facilitator is enabled with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams (meetings)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Facilitator will monitor meeting conversations in real time to detect implicit or explicit information needs.
  • When a knowledge gap is identified, Facilitator performs a web search and posts a response in the meeting chat: 
  • Responses are infrequent in practice and typically occur less than once per meeting.
  • Responses are limited to questions relevant to the meeting discussion based on agenda signals and conversational context.
  • Facilitator must be manually added to the meeting and is not enabled by default.
  • A user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license must enable Facilitator for the meeting. Other participants do not need to be licensed to receive responses.
  • Admins can disable Facilitator at the tenant level. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting. If web search is disabled, responses are not generated.
  • Users can stop the behavior at any time by removing Facilitator from the meeting.
  • The feature is supported in standard Teams meetings only and not supported in calls, webinars, or town halls.
  • The experience is supported in meetings that include external or cross-tenant participants.

[Action Required/Recommendations]

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review your organization’s Copilot web search and Facilitator configuration settings to confirm alignment with your policies.
  • Inform helpdesk and users about proactive Facilitator responses in meeting chats.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you reference Teams meeting experiences.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Facilitator uses AI to interpret meeting content and generate contextual responses during meetings.
Does the change provide end users with a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users receive proactive, AI-generated responses within the Teams meeting chat without needing to prompt the system.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated October 15, 2026: We are still finalizing rollout dates. Please update your settings by the first week of November to avoid any interruption. We will announce via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for the inconvenience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. This change only impacts tenants who have not adjusted the policy that controls file attachment in an external Teams chat. To opt out of this change, disable the capability using the Teams PowerShell setting provided in the “Action required and recommendations” section below. This can be done before the rollout and your policy setting will be respected. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions. 

Prior to this change, when existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies allow, users can already share files in external chats by sharing a link to the file. This update makes that flow easier by adding the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences directly in Teams. Files uploaded from the user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while cloud files remain stored in their existing location. Teams then assigns permissions to chat participants, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing policies. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control.

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: We will announce via Message center when we are ready to proceed.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will announce via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • This change applies only to organizations where the setting has not been explicitly configured. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted. 
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants, unless your organization has previously explicitly disabled this setting in Teams. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach and share files using the paperclip option or drag and drop in external (federated) chats.
  • Files shared through these experiences continue to be stored and shared through OneDrive or SharePoint. Files uploaded from a user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while existing cloud files remain in their current location. 
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using paperclip or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files shared through the paperclip or drag-and-drop experience.
  • The files will be shared as hyperlinks after send. 
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

To opt out of this change, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting if you have not already explicitly configured this setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns chat participants access to files shared via paperclip icon, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform – Deprecation of temporary authentication URLs for the Word Online (Business) connector
item.description:
On October 14, 2026, the Word Online (Business) connector will remove its dependency on temporary, pre-authorized download URLs. This change improves the security for file access in SharePoint and OneDrive scenarios by requiring authenticated access for generated document content.

How does this affect me?
After this change, connector actions will use authenticated access to retrieve files instead of unauthenticated download URLs. This will affect organizations using the Word Online (Business) connector in Power Automate, Power Apps, or related SharePoint and OneDrive scenarios. Additionally, makers and admins with flows or integrations that depend on unauthenticated temporary or pre-authorized download URLs returned by connector actions will also be affected by this.

With this change:
  • The connector will remove its dependency on temporary or pre-authorized download URLs.
  • Flows relying on the CreateWordFileWithContent returned URL as an unauthenticated direct download link may be impacted. It is recommended that customers should review any flows that depend on the returned URL for unauthenticated file access.
The following actions are not expected to introduce any breaking changes as these operations already retrieve content using authenticated access:
  • GetSchema
  • GetFile: The connector will retrieve content using authenticated access.
  • ConvertFile / GetFilePDF: The connector will use authenticated streaming instead of a pre-authorized download URL.
What action do I need to take?
To prepare for this change, admins, users, and makers need to perform the following actions:
  • Use authenticated file content retrieval or appropriate SharePoint sharing links instead of unauthenticated download URLs.
  • Review flows and integrations that use Word Online (Business) connector to output URLs for unauthenticated file access.
  • For file-content scenarios, use SharePoint or OneDrive Get file content and pass the file content or bytes downstream.
  • For email attachment scenarios, use Get file content and then send the email with the file attached.
  • For sharing-link scenarios, use file metadata and create an appropriate SharePoint sharing link that matches your tenant and site sharing policies.
  • For HTTP, custom connector, Azure Function, or external service scenarios, ensure the downstream caller authenticates to SharePoint or Microsoft Graph and has permission to access the file.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
item.description:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra will soon recognize Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) as standalone multifactor authentication (MFA) factors in supported authentication scenarios.

Today, WHfB and macOS PSSO can satisfy MFA requirements during primary sign-in, but users may still be required to register and use an additional passkey or authentication method for certain step-up authentication prompts, Authentication Strength policies, and sign-in frequency checks.

After this rollout, users who authenticate with WHfB or macOS PSSO will be able to satisfy supported MFA requirements without registering an additional passkey. This change helps organizations expand the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods and reduce reliance on less secure authentication methods. As part of this change, a user's WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials will be displayed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete in mid-December 2026 (previously late November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID
  • Users who authenticate with Windows Hello for Business
  • Users who authenticate with macOS Platform SSO
  • Organizations using Conditional Access Authentication Strength policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Conditional Access
  • Authentication Strength policies

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users signing in with WHfB or macOS PSSO can complete supported MFA challenges without requiring a separate passkey.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO will satisfy supported MFA requirements for step-up authentication scenarios.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported Authentication Strength policy requirements.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported sign-in frequency challenge requirements.
  • Users whose only MFA method is WHfB or macOS PSSO will be considered MFA-capable.
  • Users who sign in with only a password will no longer be automatically prompted to register an additional MFA method if WHfB or macOS PSSO is their only registered MFA credential.
  • Users with WHfB or macOS PSSO credentials, will be able to see them listed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Action required and recommendations]

No configuration changes are required.

We recommend reviewing user onboarding and MFA registration processes before rollout. Because WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials are device-bound, users may not be able to complete MFA challenges from devices where those credentials are not available.

Recommended actions:

  • Update onboarding guidance to ensure users register at least one portable MFA method.
  • Consider requiring users to register a synced passkey or Microsoft Authenticator passkey in addition to WHfB or macOS PSSO.
  • Review custom Authentication Strength policies to confirm WHfB and macOS PSSO are allowed where appropriate.
  • Update user documentation because users with only WHfB or macOS PSSO registered will no longer be automatically guided to register an additional MFA method.

Learn more (To be updated closer to GA rollout.)

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Schedule prompts in Agent Builder
item.description:

[Introduction]

We’re introducing the ability to create workflows that schedule prompts in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot. This new capability allows users to schedule prompts that run automatically on a defined cadence, such as hourly, daily, or weekly. Based on customer feedback requesting more automation and proactive insights, workflows help users reduce manual prompting and automate routine tasks using their Copilot agents.

[When this will happen]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout is expected to begin end of October 2026 (previously early September) and complete by end of November 2026 (previously end of September).

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who create and manage agents using Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

What will happen

  • Users will be able to create scheduled workflows for agents.
  • Scheduled workflows include:
    • Prompt text
    • Triggers and recurrence patterns
    • Date, time, and time zone settings
  • Supported recurrence patterns:
    • Hourly
    • Daily
    • Weekly
    • Monthly
    • Yearly
  • Workflows are configured per user and run only for the user who created them.
  • Workflows are not shared when an agent is shared with others.
  • Scheduled workflows will not run for draft or unpublished agents.
  • Users can view, edit, preview, and delete workflows within Agent Builder.
  • This feature is enabled by default and respects existing tenant and Copilot policies.

Screenshot of Agent Builder showing a “Project Horizon” agent configuration screen. The instructions panel is visible in the center, while a dropdown menu in the top-right corner is expanded with options including “Create a workflow for this agent” and “Manage workflows.” A purple arrow highlights the option to create a new workflow.

 

Screenshot of Agent Builder showing a “Project Horizon” agent configuration screen. A modal titled “Create a workflow to prompt your agent” is centered, with a text field labeled “Prompt” and scheduling options set to run weekly on Friday at 1:30 PM. A purple arrow highlights where to enter the prompt. 

[What you can do to prepare]

  • Consider informing users who build Copilot agents about the availability of workflows.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you support Copilot agent creation.
  • For privacy or compliance requests, continue using the existing Data Subject Request (DSR) processes.

Learn more: Dsr Compliance - Delete Flow | Dsr Compliance | Power Platform API | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Existing customer data may be processed automatically based on a time-based trigger rather than direct user initiation. The scope of data access remains unchanged and follows existing permissions.
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, ML, or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. This change introduces a new agent capability that allows Copilot agents to run prompts automatically on a defined schedule, instead of only responding to manual prompts.
Does this change provide a new way for users to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can now interact with generative AI asynchronously through scheduled workflows that execute prompts on their behalf.

[What and why]

Users can customize reports by specifying items such as audience, tone, length, reporting period, and report sections before reviewing and refining the generated content.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout has completed.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations who have Planner agent enabled as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Within those organizations, users with an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license who use Planner Agent.
    • Note: Users who view or edit reports do not require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license; a Copilot license is required only to generate reports.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Planner
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Planner Agent will be able to generate AI-powered status reports from Planner plan data within Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Reports will be generated only from Planner content that users already have permission to access. Existing Planner sharing permissions, Copilot policies, and agent controls continue to apply.
  • Reports will synthesize plan information, including tasks, owners, due dates, status, buckets, and recent activity, into sections such as executive summary, progress, risks and blockers, achievements, milestones, and next steps.
  • Users can customize reports by reporting period, sections, tone, length, audience, and additional instructions before reviewing and refining the generated content.
  • Reports can be exported to a Copilot Page and shared by link or exported to Word and PDF.
  • This feature adds new functionality and does not replace existing Planner capabilities.

Copilot-generated status report

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Confirm that intended users have an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Review Planner Agent and Copilot agent availability and settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. If needed, the agent can be blocked tenant-wide.
  • Inform support teams and users about the new status report generating capability, which can be accessed via the Planner Agent in Copilot or the Reports tab in Planner.
    • Note that generating a report requires a plan that is shared with a Microsoft 365 Group and contains sufficient task data.
  • Update internal documentation, training, and change management materials as appropriate.

[Compliance considerations]

To assist our customers with identifying compliance concerns, review the questions below and provide details for impact if appropriate:

  • Does the change store new customer data?
    • [Answer] Yes. A status report generated from your plan appears in the Microsoft 365 Copilot conversation. If a user chooses to export it, the report is also saved as a copilot page or a word document.
  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?
    • [Answer] Yes. When an authorized user requests a report, Planner Agent uses information from a plan they can access to create a status report. If the user attaches a file as a template, that file will also be used for the request. This change does not edit the source plan or its tasks.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?
    • [Answer] Yes. It adds the ability to generate and refine a status report through Planner Agent chat using accessible plan information. It does not grant the agent access to plans the requesting user cannot access.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra: Changes to AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission for agent identities
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Entra Agent ID is enforcing tighter restrictions for autonomous creation of an agent’s own identities. Currently, all agents are granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager upon creation without administrator approval. Starting November 4, Microsoft Entra will no longer automatically grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprint principals, and creation of identities will need an admin to grant consent.

Agents that use app-only authentication to create their own agent identities must be explicitly granted the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission or move to another supported authorization model before enforcement reaches their tenant.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra 
  • No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

Today, an agent blueprint principal is granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager automatically. This implicit grant allows the principal to create agent identities without a tenant-admin granting an app-role assignment.

After enforcement, an administrator must grant the Microsoft Graph application permission AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agents that needs this authority.

This change:

  • Makes app-only agent identity creation authority visible, auditable, and revocable.
  • Makes AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager revocable if consented
  • Affects existing and future agents.
  • Doesn't remove existing agent identities or agent blueprints.
  • Doesn't remove the ability for agent identity blueprints to create agent identities, when AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager is explicitly granted by an administrator
  • Doesn't affect an agent that uses a directory role to authorize creation of agent identities.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Identify agents that create agent identities without a signed-in user.

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Audit Logs.
  3. Set the Category to "ApplicationManagement"
  4. Set the Activity filter to "Add Service Principal"

Find events where the Initiated By (actor) Type is Application and the Target is an agent identity.

For each affected agent:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Agent blueprints>Search for your agent blueprint>Granted permissions
  3. Review if the Agent has any other granted permissions that may allow for creation of agent identities. If there are no other permissions allowing for creation, this agent relies on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager.
  4. Starting October 16, you may grant the explicit AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission through tenant-wide admin consent or manual app-role creation. Granting it earlier will cause an error. A successful grant appears in the Granted Permissions table with “An administrator” in the Granted By column.
  5. Test app-only agent identity creation before enforcement begins.
  6. Update operational guidance for a failed request after enforcement.

If an app-only request relies only on the automatic grant after enforcement reaches your tenant, the request will fail with a 403 authorization error.

Learn more

  • For more about how to grant your agents access to resources, visit Grant agents access to Microsoft 365 resources | Microsoft Learn. 
  • For the Microsoft Graph permission reference on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager, visit Microsoft Graph permissions reference - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn.

[Compliance considerations]

No specific compliance impacts have been identified for this configuration update.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Agent 365: Expanded access to Microsoft agent usage and activity insights in Microsoft 365 admin center

This change is limited to observability metrics. It does not remove licensing requirements for other Agent 365 capabilities or for agent activity metrics for agents built on third-party platforms.

[Rollout schedule]

[Impact on your organization]

  • Organizations using supported agents built by Microsoft or on Microsoft platforms

Platforms and services

  • Agent 365 observability

What will happen

  • An Agent 365 license will no longer be required to view usage and activity metrics for supported agents built by Microsoft or on Microsoft platforms.
  • The change applies to both existing and new supported agents.
  • In Registry, the affected usage and activity columns are Active users, Total sessions, Exception rate, and Run Time.
  • In Agent overview, affected cards and charts include Active users, Active users over time, and Trending agents by active users. These views may already be visible in organizations without an Agent 365 license. Reported values and trends may change temporarily as activity data accumulates during rollout.

  • As the change reaches your organization, some metrics may initially appear lower or show incomplete trends while activity data is collected. This temporary change does not necessarily indicate reduced agent usage.
  • Allow up to 30 days after data collection begins for a full 30-day reporting view for each enabled agent or platform. Completing the rollout does not mean every agent will immediately have a full 30-day history.
  • Data availability continues to depend on the agent or platform sending activity data and on applicable observability settings.
  • Existing licensing and access requirements for third-party agent observability are unchanged.
  • Other licensed Agent 365 capabilities, including risk-related features, continue to require the applicable license.

[Action required and recommendations]

When comparing usage before and after rollout, account for the time required to collect a full reporting window rather than interpreting a lower displayed value alone as a decline in usage.

Review the affected Microsoft 365 admin center views as the change reaches your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Dynamics 365 and Power Platform– Information about storage validation for Dataverse-only tenants
item.description:
Beginning November 9, 2026, we are introducing staged storage validation for supported Dynamics 365 applications. The change gives administrators clearer visibility into storage use, advance notice of potential restrictions, and several ways to remain within capacity, including removing unneeded data, adding capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

If no corrective action is initiated after repeated notifications, when a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 90 days from the date the tenant exceeds capacity, affected sandbox environments will be disabled and will no longer be accessible to users. During this phase customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed.

Production environments are not subject to administration mode and disabled stage restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox or production type environments will remain blocked while the tenant is over capacity.

Deployment Timeline:
  • Rollout begins: November 9, 2026
  • Rollout completion: December 14, 2026
How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The following products are included in the storage validation rollout:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox and production type environments are blocked immediately when the tenant exceeds its entitled capacity.
2. Administration mode After 30 unresolved days from T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 90 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from accessing *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery after remediation. During this phase, customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed. All other mechanisms designed to resolve overage are also available to customers at this phase.

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant’s current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, future restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Restrictions are removed after the tenant has returned below 100% of its entitled storage capacity. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

What action do I need to take?
Review your environment(s) and perform the following actions before November 9, 2026:
  • Review Database, File, and Log capacity in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Remove or archive data that is no longer needed.
  • Establish data governance policies in your environment to help prevent future storage overages.
  • Purchase additional capacity or configure pay-as-you-go.
  • Inform administrators, makers, and users about the potential restrictions.
  • Review your release activities that depend on sandbox availability, and plan accordingly.
For additional information, please visit the following articles:
  • What happens when my organization exceeds storage capacity?
  • Dataverse capacity-based storage details
  • Manage data with Dataverse governance policies
  • Free up storage space
  • Add more Dataverse capacity
  • Configure pay-as-you-go in your environment
  • What environments consume tenant capacity
  • Power Platform licensing guidance
*Affected environments: Sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go enabled. Any references to affected environments in this message apply exclusively to those sandbox environments.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview Audit
  • Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API
  • Exchange PowerShell Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet

  • Admins with the required permissions will be able to programmatically access audit logs through the Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API.
  • Existing PowerShell scripts, applications, and automation workflows that call Search-UnifiedAuditLog will need to be updated to use the AuditLogQuery API.

  • On October 15, 2027, Search-UnifiedAuditLog will no longer provide access to the audit log.
