  • All content in memory files is AI-generated. No raw transcript snippets are stored.
  • Memory generation requires all of the following:
    • Meeting memory is enabled for your organization.
    • Intelligent Recap is enabled for the meeting.
  • Memory files are not created for:
    • Meetings with sensitivity labels that include encryption
    • End-to-end encrypted meetings
    • Meetings with restricted copying or forwarding
  • Access and data protection:
    • Only users with access to the meeting can receive responses grounded in its memory and AI tools do not surface insights to users who do not have meeting access.
    • Memory knowledge is only shared with users who are in the same tenant as the meeting organizer.

[Action Required / Recommendations]

No immediate action is required. However, administrators should review configuration settings and consider organizational policy alignment.

Admins can enable or disable this feature in the Teams admin center.

Recommended actions:

  • Review the AI archive setting in Teams admin center before rollout. Setting path: Meeting Policies > Meeting Memory".
  • Evaluate the default expiration period, which is set to five years (1,825 days), and adjust retention settings as needed to align with compliance policies.
  • Communicate this capability to helpdesk teams and compliance stakeholders.
  • Monitor availability of the memory setting in Teams admin center and review or update settings when they become available. Memory file generation will begin 4 weeks after the setting is released to your organization.

Learn more: AI Archives for Microsoft Teams Meetings | Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn 

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data, and if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. The change introduces AI-generated meeting memory files that are stored in a tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded container and retained according to a configurable retention period.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Meeting transcripts and metadata are processed into structured AI memory files that enable downstream AI systems such as Copilot and Facilitator to reason over meeting content.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot and Facilitator use AI meeting memory files to generate context-aware responses grounded in prior meeting content.
Does the change provide users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Copilot and Facilitator, which leverage meeting memory  data to answer questions and provide insights about meetings.
Does the change modify retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. AI meeting memory files are governed by a default retention period of five years and are automatically deleted upon expiration.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Administrators can enable or disable AI meeting memory generation and configure retention settings in the Teams Admin Center.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365
item.description:
Updated October 12, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why:]

We are evolving Microsoft Copilot to better connect the tools people rely on with the capablities they need to build, customize, and scale AI across work. Updates include a new Home experience and enhanced Office capabilities in the Copilot app; Code and Autopilot for building solutions and automating work; an enterprise-grade platform for running code; and updates to Copilot Notebooks, Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive, and Work IQ.

[Impact on your organization:]

Home in the Copilot app:

  • When users open the Copilot app, they will land in Home, which brings Chat and Cowork together on one screen. Users can switch between Chat and Cowork in the prompt box. Read more in the blog. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • As part of this update, we are making the following updates to the left navigation pane: 1) Plugins will replace the standalone Agents entry point (called Agents & Skills for some preview users) from Chat and the Customize entry point from Cowork. 2) For users with access to Cowork, Automations from Cowork will move to the Home navigation pane. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • Researcher and Analyst will no longer be pinned by default in the Copilot app navigation pane. Users can continue to access these agents from Plugins and can pin them to the navigation pane based on their preferences. Organizations that want these agents to remain pinned for their users can pre-pin them through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Chat can complete long-running, multi-step knowledge work, including drafting email, managing meetings, working in Teams, managing OneDrive and SharePoint files, finding people, and creating Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and HTML files. Sensitive actions require user approval. Users can track and manage their long-running activity from Chat in the Tasks view, accessible in the upper right of the Copilot app navigation pane. These capabilities will roll out to Frontier later this month and are available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Chat will begin surfacing Skills that are used while generating responses, giving users greater transparency into how Copilot responds. This update will begin worldwide rollout in October and is available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Code:

  • The new Code experience gives users a dedicated place in the Copilot app to create trackers, dashboards, and apps using natural language. Users can access Code by going to the Code tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Code uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • Code is rolling out to Frontier later this month.
  • To prepare: To enable Copilot Code for your tenant, admin must deploy the unified app and set the target channel to beta.

Autopilot:

  • Autopilot, previously called Scout, is an always-on personal agent in the Copilot app with persistent context, identity, and memory. Users can access Autopilot by going to the Autopilot tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Autopilot uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • We will update this message with rollout timing and admin control details when available.

Copilot app UI updates:

  • Cowork, Code, and Autopilot entry points in the Copilot app will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Users that do not have a spending policy enabled will not be able to access these capabilities; instead, they will see an in-product message after clicking on the entry points to request access or learn more.
  • A new Microsoft 365 admin center setting will let admins choose whether users without a spending policy see Request Access or Learn More. Admins can configure whether or not users can request Copilot credits to use these experiences. Admins can also choose to block requests.
  • The existing setting in the admin center used to hide usage-based experiences (“Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing”) will be removed.
  • By default, enterprise users without a spending policy will see the “request access” message. Education users will see a Learn More link and cannot request access.
  • This update will roll out to standard customers in October and deferred customers in November.
  • To prepare: Review Microsoft 365 Admin center settings for usage-based experiences and spending policy. Decide if you want users without a spending policy to receive a "Request access" or "Learn more" message.

Full Office capabilities in the Copilot app:

  • Users can use full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint creation, editing, and collaboration capabilities in the Copilot app, side by side with Copilot. Users can also access recent Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files from Library in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Capabilities accessed through Chat are included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license. Capabilities accessed through Cowork use usage-based billing.
  • These capabilities are rolling out to Frontier later this month.

Copilot Managed Runtime:

  • Copilot Managed Runtime is an enterprise-grade platform for running code within the Microsoft 365 tenant boundary under IT governance. It supports apps built in Code, Cowork, Copilot Studio, and supported command-line and SDK experiences. Admins can manage these apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Read more in the blog.
  • Managed Runtime is starting to roll out now into public preview.

Copilot Notebooks updates:

  • Copilot Notebooks will add task delegation, full Office editing and collaboration, interactive report creation, audio overview updates, model selection, and an updated user experience in the Copilot app and OneNote.
  • These updates will roll out to Frontier later this month.

SharePoint and OneDrive updates:

  • We are announcing the general availability of Copilot in SharePoint. The everyday AI capabilities that have been in public preview stay included with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). New agentic capabilities and the ability to work at greater scale than was possible in preview will be available through usage-based billing (UBB) and consume Copilot Credits. We are also introducing general availability of Copilot in OneDrive, which follows the same licensing structure as SharePoint. Read more about Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive in the blog.
  • General availability begins rolling out later this month. Tenant availability may follow as rollout progresses.
  • To prepare: No action is required to continue using capabilities included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). Admins can control who can access advanced SharePoint capabilities through UBB by going to Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management. Existing cost management policies may automatically include newly available services. Existing PowerShell opt-out settings for the Public Preview of Copilot in SharePoint will continue to be honored until November 1st; after that, manage availability through SharePoint site AI settings.

Business Applications in Work IQ:

  • Work IQ now includes Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Power Platform data, enabling Copilot to ground responses and tasks on business and productivity data. Read more in the blog.
  • These updates will start rolling out in public preview later this month.
  • To prepare: Admins can configure Dynamics 365 and Power Platform data sources for Copilot in the Power Platform admin center. Admins can also manage the availability of business applications in Copilot in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings, and access through the Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) under Agents > Tools.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

In addition to the guidance listed in the individual updates above:

  • A spending policy is required for users to access capabilities available through Usage-based billing. Enable Copilot Credit consumption and configure spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management. Educate users about usage-based billing scenarios and how to request access through IT. Learn more about spending policy and usage-based billing in the blog and message center post titled: Evolving Copilot pricing and new FinOps capabilities for AI.
  • Monitor this post for updated availability and deployment details.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Channel agent orchestration with GitHub, Asana, and Jira via Model Context Protocol (MCP)
item.description:
Updated August 20, 2026: We have paused rollout of this feature at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

Microsoft is introducing a new capability in Teams that enables Channel Agent to orchestrate tasks with select third-party Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, including GitHub, Asana, and Atlassian (JIRA). This integration supports collaborative workflows that reflect real human teamwork, allowing agents to transparently reason through tasks and gather information across tools. This change helps reduce manual switching between apps and improves task completion efficiency—all within the familiar Teams environment.

A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to use this feature.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 515466.

When this will happen
  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Begins in mid-November 2025 and is expected to complete by end of July 2026 (previously late January).
  • General Availability: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. 
How this affects your organization

Who is affected: Microsoft 365 tenants using Teams and Channel Agent integrations.

What will happen:

  • Channel Agent will be able to collaborate with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers like GitHub, Asana, and Jira.
  • Users can ask Channel Agent questions and receive coordinated responses across tools:

          Screenshot 1

    Screenshot 2

  • The feature will be available in preview and requires admin enablement.
  • A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required.
  • There is no impact unless enabled by tenant admins.

What you can do to prepare

  • Enable Channel Agent usage in Teams for your tenant.
  • Allow apps that integrate with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers such as GitHub, Asana, or Jira.
  • Ensure users who need access have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Review internal documentation and update helpdesk guidance as needed.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.
